questions.q: What does Salesforce typically create when a rep converts a Lead?
options: Only a new Lead with a different status
An Account, a Contact, and usually an Opportunity
questions.explain: Lead conversion creates an Account and a Contact, and (unless skipped) an Opportunity.

questions.q: Which report type helps you see where converted leads ended up?
questions.explain: Leads with Converted Lead Information exposes the converted account, contact, and opportunity for each lead.

questions.q: In SOQL, how do you reach a parent record's field, such as the account name from an opportunity?
questions.explain: SOQL follows child-to-parent relationships with dot notation, such as Account.Name or Owner.Name.

questions.q: Why check for leads that are converted but have no ConvertedOpportunityId?
options: Because Salesforce deletes those leads automatically
Because those leads always have the highest amounts
Because conversion can skip creating an opportunity, so those leads never enter pipeline
Because SOQL cannot query converted leads
questions.explain: Reps can convert without creating an opportunity. Those conversions inflate conversion counts but produce no pipeline.

questions.q: Which technique lists opportunities that have no contact roles at all?
options: A subquery anti-join: WHERE Id NOT IN (SELECT OpportunityId FROM OpportunityContactRole)
questions.explain: A NOT IN subquery against OpportunityContactRole returns opportunities with no matching role records.
